programs.title: National Astronomy Week 2026
programs.text: A week of telescopes, talks, and stargazing across 5 Ugandan cities.
programs.description: National Astronomy Week 2026 brings telescope nights, public lectures, and sky-watching activities to Kampala, Mbarara, Gulu, Jinja, and Fort Portal. Organized by the Uganda Astronomical Society with support from StellarView Technologies, the week aims to spark public interest in astronomy and highlight Uganda's unique equatorial advantage for stargazing.
outcomes: New astronomy clubs established at 3 universities

programs.title: CubeSat Build Series
programs.text: Monthly hands-on workshops building Uganda's first university CubeSat.
programs.description: A structured series of monthly workshops where university students design, prototype, and test subsystems for Uganda's first university CubeSat. Sessions cover mission design, power systems,通信通信通信通信通信通信通信, and thermal control, culminating in a flight-ready satellite model by December 2026.

programs.title: Space Outreach Tour
programs.text: Bringing space education to schools across all 4 regions of Uganda.
programs.description: A nationwide outreach tour visiting secondary schools in all four regions of Uganda. Each visit includes interactive sessions on satellite technology, hands-on rocket-building activities, and career talks with space professionals, inspiring the next generation of Ugandan scientists and engineers.
outcomes: 15 student teams formed for rocketry challenge

programs.title: World Space Week Uganda 2026
programs.text: The national World Space Week campaign, connecting Rocket Revolution to astronomy, Earth observation, and local innovation.
programs.description: Uganda's flagship World Space Week celebration under the global theme 'Rocket Revolution'. Activities span all four regions with rocketry demonstrations, stargazing nights, policy panels, school outreach, and the Innovation Showcase. Partners include NOA's Quest, Uganda Astronomical Society, and StellarView Technologies.

programs.title: Uganda Earth Observation Initiative
programs.text: Building local capacity for satellite-based Earth observation, data analysis, and applications in agriculture and environment.
programs.description: A two-year initiative to train Ugandan researchers and technicians in Earth observation data analysis using Sentinel-2 and Landsat imagery. The program focuses on agricultural monitoring, deforestation tracking, and water resource management, with applications directly benefiting Uganda's rural communities.
outcomes: 30 researchers trained in EO data analysis
3 pilot applications in agriculture and environment

programs.title: Space for Schools — Teacher Training
programs.text: Training secondary school teachers across Uganda to integrate space science and astronomy into the curriculum.
programs.description: A comprehensive teacher training program equipping secondary school educators with the knowledge and materials to teach space science, astronomy, and satellite technology. Teachers receive curriculum guides, activity kits, and ongoing mentorship support from Uganda's space community.
outcomes: New curriculum module approved by NCPE
Teacher network established for ongoing support

programs.title: East African CubeSat Challenge
programs.text: A regional CubeSat design competition for university students across East Africa.
programs.description: A competitive program challenging university teams from Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda, and Uganda to design, build, and test a functional CubeSat payload. The challenge includes mentorship from international partners, technical reviews, and a final launch opportunity for the winning team.

programs.title: CanSat Uganda Program
programs.text: CanSat satellite simulation program inspiring young innovators through hands-on space engineering education.
programs.description: CanSat Uganda introduces students to satellite engineering through a simulate-and-build approach where teams design, construct, and deploy a soda-can-sized satellite. The program follows the international CanSat competition framework and has been led by Derrick Tebusweke since 2024.

programs.title: AfDev-Sat Joint Satellite Mission
programs.text: Africa's first jointly-built satellite. Egypt, Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Sudan, and Uganda collaborating on Earth observation.
programs.description: The African Development Satellite (AfDev-Sat) is a historic pan-African initiative where six nations — Egypt, Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Sudan, and Uganda — are jointly designing and building Africa's first collaboratively constructed satellite. The mission focuses on Earth observation for climate monitoring and agricultural applications.

announcements.title: Space Uganda Opens As A Year-Round Umbrella
announcements.excerpt: The ecosystem is organising under one national domain for communities, campaigns, partners, and public opportunities.
announcements.body: Uganda's space community has a new national home. Space Uganda launches as a year-round platform connecting researchers, students, engineers, and organizations across the country's growing space ecosystem. The platform provides a unified portal for events, knowledge sharing, opportunities, and community collaboration, replacing fragmented efforts with a single coordinated national resource.
announcements.author: Ronnie Atuhaire

announcements.title: WSW Uganda 2026 Theme Confirmed
announcements.excerpt: World Space Week 2026 will run under the global theme Rocket Revolution from October 4-10.

Uganda's national celebration will feature rocketry demonstrations, stargazing events, policy panels, and school outreach activities across all four regions, with the flagship day on October 10 in Kampala.

knowledge.title: Earth Observation Applications for Uganda's Agricultural Sector
knowledge.author: Dr. Sarah Nabukenya
knowledge.summary: Analysis of satellite-based crop monitoring techniques and their applicability to Uganda's smallholder farming systems.
knowledge.body: This paper examines how satellite-based remote sensing technologies can be applied to monitor crop health and agricultural productivity across Uganda's diverse farming regions. Using Sentinel-2 and Landsat imagery, the study demonstrates that NDVI analysis can effectively identify crop stress patterns, enabling timely interventions for smallholder farmers. The research includes case studies from three agricultural zones and provides a framework for integrating EO data into national food security monitoring systems.

knowledge.title: CubeSat Design Considerations for East African Climate Monitoring
knowledge.author: James Okello
knowledge.summary: Technical specifications and mission planning for a CubeSat constellation targeting East African weather patterns.
knowledge.body: This technical paper presents the design considerations for a CubeSat constellation specifically tailored for climate monitoring in East Africa. The study covers orbital mechanics, payload selection, power systems, and communication architecture suitable for regional weather pattern observation. Simulation results show that a 3-unit CubeSat constellation in low Earth orbit could provide daily revisit times over the Lake Victoria basin, significantly improving weather forecasting capabilities.

knowledge.title: Uganda's National Space Policy Framework
knowledge.author: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation
knowledge.summary: Draft national policy framework for space activities, satellite licensing, and data sharing in Uganda.
knowledge.body: The draft National Space Policy Framework establishes Uganda's regulatory environment for space activities, including satellite licensing, frequency coordination, and data sharing protocols. The document outlines institutional responsibilities, defines the role of the proposed Uganda Space Agency, and aligns national policy with international space treaties and African Union space initiatives. Public consultation is open through March 2026.

knowledge.title: Building a Distributed Ground Station Network in Uganda
knowledge.author: Navneet Singh
knowledge.summary: Step-by-step guide to setting up low-cost ground stations for satellite communication across Ugandan universities.
knowledge.body: This practical guide provides detailed instructions for establishing low-cost satellite ground stations at Ugandan universities. Covering hardware selection, antenna design, software configuration, and operational procedures, the guide enables institutions to participate in satellite communication with minimal investment. The guide includes a bill of materials, assembly diagrams, and troubleshooting guides based on the three pilot stations established at Makerere, Kyambogo, and Mbarara universities.

knowledge.title: Public Astronomy Outreach: A Practical Handbook for Uganda
knowledge.author: Zoora Harrison
knowledge.summary: How to organize telescope nights, school visits, and community astronomy events across Uganda.
knowledge.body: A comprehensive handbook for organizing public astronomy events in Uganda, from telescope nights at schools to community stargazing sessions. The guide covers equipment selection, volunteer training, site selection for optimal viewing, and engagement strategies for diverse audiences. Includes templates for event planning, safety protocols, and promotional materials, based on StellarView Technologies' experience running 42 astronomy events across 8 countries.

knowledge.title: Using Sentinel-2 Data for Crop Health Monitoring in Uganda
knowledge.author: Uganda National Meteorology Authority
knowledge.summary: Open dataset of processed Sentinel-2 imagery covering Uganda's major agricultural zones with NDVI indices.
knowledge.body: This open-access dataset contains processed Sentinel-2 satellite imagery covering Uganda's major agricultural zones, including the Teso, Busoga, and Buganda regions. Each image tile includes calculated NDVI indices, cloud-masked composites, and metadata for use in crop health monitoring applications. The dataset is updated monthly and covers the period from January 2024 to present, providing a valuable resource for agricultural researchers and food security analysts.

knowledge.title: Introduction to Model Rocketry for Ugandan Students
knowledge.author: Twesigye Duncan
knowledge.summary: Beginner-friendly course covering rocket physics, building techniques, and safe launch procedures.
knowledge.body: A beginner-friendly course material designed for Ugandan secondary and university students interested in model rocketry. The course covers fundamental physics of rocket flight, materials and construction techniques, safety protocols, and launch procedures. Includes practical exercises, building templates, and assessment quizzes. The material has been tested with over 60 students across 8 schools in the Kampala and Wakiso regions.

knowledge.title: Space Law and Governance in Africa: Challenges and Opportunities
knowledge.author: Angu'zu Raymond
knowledge.summary: Comparative analysis of space legislation across African nations with recommendations for Uganda.
knowledge.body: This paper provides a comparative analysis of space legislation across 12 African nations, examining regulatory frameworks, institutional structures, and policy gaps. The study identifies key challenges including频谱 coordination, debris mitigation, and data sovereignty, while highlighting opportunities for regional cooperation through the African Union. Recommendations for Uganda's emerging space policy include harmonization with the African Space Agency framework and establishment of a national space coordination body.

knowledge.title: GIS and Satellite Imagery for Urban Planning in Kampala
knowledge.author: Grace Lydia Nabbaale
knowledge.summary: How satellite imagery and GIS tools are being used to inform urban development decisions in Kampala Metropolitan Area.
knowledge.body: This case study examines the application of GIS and satellite imagery in urban planning for the Kampala Metropolitan Area. Using high-resolution satellite data and GIS analysis, the study maps land use changes, identifies informal settlements, and assesses infrastructure gaps. The findings demonstrate how remote sensing tools can support evidence-based urban planning decisions, with specific applications for transportation planning, green space management, and disaster risk reduction in Kampala.

knowledge.title: Astrophotography from the Equator: Capturing Uganda's Night Sky
knowledge.author: Dr Malcom Chris B
knowledge.summary: Tips and techniques for photographing the Milky Way, Southern Cross, and equatorial constellations from Uganda.
knowledge.body: A practical guide to capturing stunning images of Uganda's equatorial night sky. The guide covers camera settings, equipment recommendations, and composition techniques for photographing the Milky Way, Southern Cross, and other prominent constellations visible from Uganda's latitude. Includes specific location recommendations within Uganda, seasonal shooting calendars, and post-processing workflows for both smartphone and DSLR photographers.

faq.question: What is the Uganda Space Community?

answers.author: Ronnie Atuhaire
answers.text: The Uganda Space Community (USC) is the national platform connecting researchers, students, engineers, policymakers, and organizations working in Uganda's space sector. It serves as a hub for collaboration, knowledge sharing, and community building, with over 340 members across 4 regional chapters.

answers.author: Zoora Harrison
answers.text: USC is a community-driven initiative that brings together everyone interested in space science and technology in Uganda — from university students to established researchers and industry professionals. Our platform provides events, knowledge resources, and networking opportunities for the entire ecosystem.

faq.question: How do I join the Uganda Space Community?

answers.author: Ronnie Atuhaire
answers.text: Click 'Log in' in the top navigation, create an account with your name, email, and password. Once registered, you can complete your profile, join working groups, and start contributing to the community. Membership is free and open to anyone interested in Uganda's space sector.

answers.author: Zoora Harrison
answers.text: Sign up at space.org.ug, fill in your profile with your interests and affiliations, and explore the community. You can immediately participate in events, submit content, and connect with other members. We recommend joining at least one community group to get started.

answers.author: Ronnie Atuhaire
answers.text: Anyone with an interest in space science, technology, or policy in Uganda. This includes students, researchers, engineers, educators, policymakers, journalists, and enthusiasts. There are no restrictions on background or qualification — our strength is in the diversity of our community.

faq.question: How do I find and attend community events?

answers.author: Ronnie Atuhaire
answers.text: Visit the Mission Calendar page to see upcoming events, workshops, and activities. Events are categorized by type (Physical, Virtual, Workshop) and you can filter by date. Many events are free and open to the public — just show up or register online.

answers.author: Halimah Bukirwa
answers.text: Follow Space Uganda on social media and check the calendar regularly. World Space Week (October 4-10) is our biggest annual event with activities across the country. We also recommend joining the community group for your region to receive local event notifications.

faq.question: How do I submit content (events, news, opportunities)?

answers.author: Ronnie Atuhaire
answers.text: Log in to your account, then use the submission forms on the relevant pages (Calendar for events, Updates for news, Launchpad for programs). All submissions go through a review process before appearing publicly — our curators typically review within 48 hours.

answers.author: Angu'zu Raymond
answers.text: Create an account, complete your profile, and you'll see 'Submit' buttons throughout the site. Submissions are reviewed by curators within 48 hours. We encourage contributions from all community members to keep our platform comprehensive and up-to-date.

faq.question: How does my organization get listed on the platform?

answers.author: Ronnie Atuhaire
answers.text: Any organization active in Uganda's space sector can be listed. Submit your organization details through the Community page 'Submit Organization' form. Include your name, category, location, and a brief description. We currently list 32 organizations across academia, government, and the private sector.

answers.author: Capt Simon Bruno
answers.text: Reach out through the contact form or email hello@space.org.ug with your organization details. We'll add you to the ecosystem map after verification. Listings are free and include your name, category, location, and a link to your website.

faq.question: How can I volunteer or contribute to Space Uganda?

answers.author: Ronnie Atuhaire
answers.text: Join the community, complete your profile, and indicate your interests. We regularly call for volunteers for events like World Space Week, STEM outreach, and research projects. You can also contribute to the Knowledge Base by submitting papers, guides, or datasets.

faq.question: What is World Space Week Uganda?

answers.author: Ronnie Atuhaire
answers.text: World Space Week Uganda is the national celebration of the UN-declared World Space Week (October 4-10). In 2026, we're running under the global theme 'Rocket Revolution' with events across all 4 regions of Uganda, including rocketry demonstrations, stargazing nights, policy panels, and school outreach.

answers.author: Zoora Harrison
answers.text: It's a week of space-related activities — from stargazing nights and rocketry workshops to policy panels and school outreach. Open to everyone, completely free. Last year's celebration attracted over 1,200 participants across 15 events in 4 cities.

faq.question: Are there regional chapters or groups?

answers.author: Ronnie Atuhaire
answers.text: Yes! The community is organized into 4 regional chapters: Central (Kampala, Wakiso, Mukono), Eastern (Jinja, Mbale), Western (Mbarara, Fort Portal), and Northern (Gulu, Lira). Each chapter has local organizers and regular activities, with the Central chapter being the most active with 96 members.

faq.question: Can I access satellite data or research through the platform?

answers.author: Navneet Singh
answers.text: The Knowledge Base contains open-access papers, datasets, tools, and guides. We're building partnerships with agencies like UNMA and RCMRD to provide access to satellite imagery and Earth observation data for Uganda. Our Sentinel-2 agricultural dataset has been downloaded over 890 times.

answers.author: Navneet Singh
answers.text: Through our Ground Station Network program, we're working toward real-time satellite data access. Three pilot stations are operational at Makerere, Kyambogo, and Mbarara universities. For now, check the Knowledge Base for available datasets and tools.
